Ontology_AssayAndWorkflow_prompt.notes: The experiment is a CX-MS (Chemical Cross-Linking Mass Spectrometry) study using BS3 and DSSO cross-linkers. While not a traditional 'tpp' (Thermal Proteome Profiling) workflow, mod_tpp is often used as a proxy for structural/interaction proteomics in some routing schemas, but the primary signal here is the specific cross-linking modifications. No labeling strategy like TMT or SILAC was used; it is a label-free DDA approach.

Ontology_TreatmentAndDesign_prompt.notes: The proteomics part of this study specifically uses chemical cross-linking mass spectrometry (CX-MS) to compare the intramolecular (cis) interaction of the TCPTP tail with its catalytic domain versus the intermolecular (trans) interaction of separate domains. While the paper discusses ITGA1 activation and various mutants, the MS data described in the methods and PRIDE metadata focuses on the cis vs trans structural comparison.
